problem: Whether the variance-scaled normalized Turán deficit V·δ_D at the first-descent index D of a Poisson–binomial pmf has a universal positive lower bound; the paper proves V·δ_D ≥ 1/4 whenever V ≥ 1.
debate: The literature on quantitative log-concavity and mode/mass structure of Bernoulli sums: Newton/Turán log-concavity via Pitman, deficit bounds of Hillion–Johnson and Johnson, Darroch's mode location, Pitman's tilted-law ratio bounds, Dümbgen–Wellner, and the maximal-mass bounds of Bobkov–Marsiglietti–Melbourne.
gap: Known lower bounds on δ_k depend on n (Hillion–Johnson's ultra-log-concavity bound) or on the success probabilities (Johnson), and they degenerate when summands with p_i near 0 or 1 pile up at fixed variance, while the mode, ratio and maximal-mass results do not control δ_k at all.
contribution: A variance-only bound V·δ_D ≥ 1/4 for V ≥ 1, with the corollary f_{D+r}/f_D ≤ exp(−r/(4V)), a binomial family showing the best constant is at most 1/3, a 1/5 bound at the rightmost mode, and transfer to real-rooted coefficient sequences such as Stirling and Eulerian rows, proved with a computer-assisted Bernstein-expansion step.
note: The theorem is clean and the gap is stated plainly, but the opening never says why anyone needs δ_D at the first descent beyond the result itself, and it never shows that the decay corollary is not already available from Pitman's tilted-law ratio bounds; fix both or reviewers will read this as a narrow, non-sharp, computer-checked constant.
